expected_key_points: REST is an architectural style for web APIs
Clients interact with resources over HTTP
Common methods include GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE
REST APIs are usually stateless
ideal_answer: A REST API is an interface based on representational state transfer where clients interact with resources over HTTP using standard methods such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE in a stateless manner.

expected_key_points: OSI has seven conceptual layers
Each layer has a specific communication responsibility
Network layer handles routing and logical addressing
Transport layer handles end-to-end delivery and reliability
Application layer supports user-facing network services
ideal_answer: The OSI model is a seven-layer networking model: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation, and application. Each layer has a specific responsibility, such as routing at the network layer and end-to-end delivery at the transport layer.

expected_key_points: An index is a data structure on one or more columns
Indexes help databases find rows faster
Indexes improve read/query performance
Indexes add storage cost and can slow writes
ideal_answer: Database indexing creates a data structure on selected columns so the database can locate rows faster during queries. It improves read speed, but adds storage cost and can slow inserts or updates.

question_text: What is polymorphism in object-oriented programming?
content: What is polymorphism in object-oriented programming?
expected_key_points: Polymorphism lets the same interface represent different behavior
Different classes can implement or override the same method
It improves flexibility and reusable design
Runtime polymorphism is commonly achieved through method overriding
ideal_answer: Polymorphism allows the same interface or method name to represent different implementations depending on the object or class being used.

question_text: What is the time complexity of binary search and why?
content: What is the time complexity of binary search and why?
expected_key_points: Binary search requires sorted data
Each comparison checks the middle element
Each step removes about half of the remaining search space
This repeated halving gives O(log n) time complexity
ideal_answer: Binary search runs in O(log n) time because it repeatedly compares against the middle element and halves the search space on each step, assuming the collection is sorted.
